ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Law of 12 November 2004 on the fight against money laundering and terrorist financing, as amended (AML/CFT Law); Law of 13 January 2019 establishing the Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE Law), as amended by the Law of 25 March 2020; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 13 January 2019 on the functioning of the RBE; Law of 10 August 1915 on commercial companies, as amended by the Law of 23 June 2016 (SARL regime); Law of 27 June 2018 on export controls covering dual-use goods and defence-related products; CSSF Regulation 12-02 and competent-authority AML/CFT doctrine implementing Directive (EU) 2015/849.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Amended Luxembourg Law of 10 August 1915 on Commercial Companies (Loi modifiée du 10 août 1915 concernant les sociétés commerciales), SARL provisions - Title II, Articles 710-1 to 710-26, as modernised by the Law of 19 December 2019; Grand-Ducal Regulation of 23 March 2021 on electronic filing; Law of 10 July 2020 on the Luxembourg Business Registers
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), Luxembourg
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Notarised Articles of Association (acte constitutif notarié) together with the unified electronic registration data form (formulaire de renseignements) filed by the notary with the RCS and published in the Recueil Électronique des Sociétés et Associations (RESA)
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: Minimum fully-subscribed and paid-in capital of EUR 12,000 (approx. USD 13,100); the full capital must be blocked in a Luxembourg-domiciled bank blocking account or deposited with the State Caisse de Consignation before the notarial deed is executed; funds are released to the Company only after RCS registration. In-kind contributions require a statutory auditor's valuation board report (rapport du réviseur d'entreprises agréé).
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED, that the founding shareholders adopt the Articles of Association of the Company as a Société à Responsabilité Limitée under the amended Law of 10 August 1915, the corporate object being the manufacture of armored tactical and all-terrain military vehicles (ISIC 3040). RESOLVED FURTHER, that the subscription and payment of the fully subscribed share capital of EUR 12,000, evidenced by the bank's blocking deposit certificate, is accepted and capitalized. RESOLVED FURTHER, that the registered office is hereby designated as [address], Luxembourg. RESOLVED, that [Name], [Name] and [Name] are appointed gérants, with all powers necessary to perfect registration before the Luxembourg Business Registers, tax and social administrations, and to procure the industry and environmental licenses.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Name verification, corporate-object legality review and drafting of the articles
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary (Chambre des Notaires du Luxembourg) with online pre-check via lbr.lu
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: File two proposed names with the notary for an availability certificate; instruct the notary to prepare the statuts and to verify that the SARL corporate object, including armored military vehicle manufacturing under ISIC 3040, is lawful and does not constitute a reserved activity without license; obtain written legal opinion on any defense-trade notification duties; settle the address, duration and audit clauses.
required_dossiers: Passport copies and proof of address of every founding shareholder and intended gérant
Draft articles of association
Shareholder agreement (if any)
Professional CVs and integrity declarations of intended gérants
Business plan for the manufacturing plant
Name availability certificate request
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the proposed name is refused, the notary files a second-choice name the same day with priority; if the corporate object is deemed sensitive, the notary narrows the drafting and refers the matter to the Ministry of the Economy's pre-licensing guidance within 5 working days.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Blocking deposit of the minimum share capital
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg credit institution of the Company's choice, or the State Caisse de Consignation
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a capital blocking account (compte bloqué) in the pending company's name or in the notary's escrow; transfer EUR 12,000 from each subscriber per the subscription schedule; ensure the bank issues an attestation of blocking; instruct the bank that release is conditional on RCS registration; for international wires, obtain SWIFT confirmations and comply with Know-Your-Customer/source-of-funds checks; if shareholders are foreign legal entities, provide their constitutive documents and proof of authority of signatories.
required_dossiers: Bank KYC file of the Company in formation
Identity and source-of-wealth documentation of shareholders
Subscription statement signed by each subscriber for his/her quota
Draft articles of association
Preliminary RCS name confirmation
Bank wire confirmations (SWIFT MT103)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank questions provenance of funds, the notary coordinates submission of notarised wealth-origin certificates, recent audited financial statements for corporate shareholders, and tax compliance attestations; alternatively deposit the funds with the Caisse de Consignation to preserve the notarial timeline.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Execution of the notarial deed of incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg notary in the district of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene the subscribers to sign the authentic deed; verify personal attendance or valid special powers of attorney for remote subscribers; the notary reads the final statuts, confirms identity of each subscriber, records acceptance of each quota, verifies the blocking certificate and the integrity of the object, and obtains the signed consent of the appointed gérants; after signature, the notary retains the deed and issues association copies (expéditions) for filing and banking purposes.
required_dossiers: Final draft articles of association
Capital blocking certificate from the bank/Caisse de Consignation
Identity documents of all present signatories
Signed subscription lists and apport reports for any in-kind contributions
Consent of each gérant to take office
Declaration of non-bankruptcy and clean criminal record of gérants
Powers of attorney for any remote subscriber (legalised and apostilled if foreign)
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a subscriber cannot attend physically, the notary accepts a certified power of attorney in Luxembourg or EU form and re-schedules execution within 48 hours; if an in-kind contribution valuation is queried, the notary orders an expedited report from a réviseur d'entreprises agréé before signing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic registration with the Luxembourg Business Registers
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) - RCS, through the notary's e-filing portal
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: The notary submits the e-registration dossier to the RCS with the authenticated deed, the uniform electronic registration form, the gérants' acceptances, proof of registered-office rights, and paid filing fees; the RCS reviews the file under its statutory control procedure; once admitted, the RCS allocates the official registration number (numéro d'immatriculation) and the entity becomes legally existing; the notary retrieves the RCS extract (extrait) and forwards it to the Company.
required_dossiers: Notarial deed original (acte constitutif)
Uniform registration form signed by the appointed gérants
Consent of the premises' owner and, where applicable, the lease
Copy of IDs of appointed gérants
Proof of payment of LBR and publication fees
Power of attorney, if a gérant is represented before the RCS
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RCS raises an unsatisfied formality, the notary submits precise clarifications or a supplementary notarial act rectifying the defect within 5 working days; in case of a substantive objection against a gérant's integrity, the shareholders appoint an alternative gérant and the notary files an amendment deed.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: RESA publication, RCS extract and beneficial-ownership registration
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR), publishing in RESA; Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: LBR publishes the incorporation notice in the RESA electronic gazette, making the deed opposable to third parties; the Company receives the conclusive RCS extract and registration number; in parallel, file the beneficial-ownership declaration in the RBE register with full voluntary construction of the ownership chain of each ultimate beneficial owner; request the LEI code through the LBR/LuxCSD channel if not yet issued.
required_dossiers: RCS registration number reference
RBE declaration form listing ultimate beneficial owners (name, DOB, nationality, ownership percentage)
Organisation chart of the ownership chain (where corporate shareholders exist)
Proof of identity of all UBOs
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the RBE query flags non-disclosure of intermediate SPVs, the Company files a consolidated chain of ownership and, if necessary, requests legal advice from a Luxembourg corporate counsel to confirm statutory exclusions; RBE acceptance is automatically linked to the RCS file.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Industrial establishment authorization, defense trade license, and tax-social registrations
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Ministère de l'Économie (via Guichet.lu), Office des Licences d'Exportation, Administration de l'enregistrement, des domaines et de la TVA (AEDT), Centre Commun de la Sécurité Sociale (CCSS)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Apply online through Guichet.lu for the business establishment permit (autorisation d'établissement) for the manufacturing activity; submit the regulated-equipment declaration under the amended Law of 27 June 1990 for armored military tactical vehicle production; complete the automatic VAT registration to obtain the TVA number, apply for the EORI number from the Customs administration, and register as employer with the CCSS upon first hire; obtain municipal integration documents if plant infrastructure is under construction.
required_dossiers: RCS extract and articles of association
Criminal record extracts (bulletin no. 3) of each gérant
Environmental operating authorization application file
Site lease or ownership title with zoning conformity certificate (certificat d'affectation)
Description of the manufacturing process listing regulated military items
Export-control compliance programme and end-user statement templates
Evidence of professional insurance and preliminary fire-safety statement
ID documents and residence proofs of the gérants
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the establishment authorization is refused, the Company may file an administrative appeal with the Minister within two months and subsequently before the Administrative Tribunal; for the defense license, a preliminary negative response can be cured by providing NATO end-user certificates or a Ministry of Defense sponsorship letter; no manufacturing operations may commence before the permit is effective.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Ministère de l'Économie - Direction de l'industrie (Ministry of the Economy, Industry Directorate) through the Guichet.lu single window; defense goods licensing coordinated with the Office des Licences d'Exportation of the Ministry of Foreign and European Affairs
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: Autorisation d'établissement (Business Establishment Permit) for the industrial production of armored tactical vehicles; separate Autorisation de fabrication et de commerce de matériel réglementé under the amended Law of 27 June 1990 for military-grade all-terrain vehicles and dual-use components

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Administration de l'environnement (Luxembourg Environmental Protection Agency)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Class A - Full Environmental Impact Assessment (EIA) and operating authorization (autorisation d'exploitation) required under the amended Law of 10 June 1999 on classified establishments, because the plant performs vehicle assembly, metal preparation, industrial painting and composite processing above the listed thresholds; the EIA is integrated with the municipal building permit and the water abstraction permit (Law of 23 October 2000, as amended)
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: Compliance with EU Industrial Emissions Directive 2010/75/EU as transposed by the Grand-Ducal Regulation of 24 March 2022; industrial wastewater discharge limits for BOD5 ≤ 25 mg/L, COD ≤ 125 mg/L, suspended solids ≤ 35 mg/L and heavy metals (Zn, Ni, Cu, Cr) per river-basin standards of the Water Management Administration (Administration de la gestion de l'eau); VOC emissions from painting lines limited to ≤ 50 mg C/Nm³ with a solvent management plan aligned to Directive 2004/42/EC threshold for vehicle finishing; hazardous wastes (paint sludge, solvent residues, armored composite off-cuts) must be labelled, classified and consigned through licensed collectors using the AGESIS waste traceability system; soil protection measures and non-dispersive storage of reactive compounds are mandatory

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: Pre-occupancy fire safety certification from the Corps grand-ducal d'incendie et de secours (CGDIS) covering fire-resistance ratings, escape routes, hydrant layout and internal gas/sprinkler installations; structural load inspection and authorization per the Eurocodes enforced by the municipal building authority; workplace safety clearance from the Inspection du travail et des mines (ITM) for mechanical hazards, pressure equipment, electrical installations and noise exposure before commissioning; where ammunition-adjacent testing is performed, an additional internal-security protocol and restricted-area protection study must be approved by the relevant ministry

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Luxembourg operates a functionally split national tax administration: (1) Administration des Contributions Directes (ACD) — competent authority for corporate income tax, municipal business tax and net wealth tax, with official portal at impotsdirects.public.lu; (2) Administration de l'Enregistrement, des Domaines et de la TVA (AEDT) — competent authority for VAT (TVA), registration duties, excise and real-estate registration, with portal at aed.public.lu; (3) Administration des Douanes et Accises — customs and export-control authority forming part of the AEDT, with portal at douane.public.lu; (4) Registre de Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS) / Luxembourg Business Registers (LBR) — national legal-entity registry, lbr.lu. All filing and registration procedures for a commercial company are coordinated through the single digital public-service portal Guichet.lu / MyGuichet (myguichet.lu).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: SOP for a foreign-owned SARL: (i) a Luxembourg notary executes the articles of association (acte constitutif) and lodges the incorporation application with the RCS/Guichet unique; (ii) the RCS issues the company's 13-digit national identification number (numéro d'identification / matricule), which is the common business key subsequently used for ACD and AEDT matters; (iii) the ACD automatically opens a corporate income-tax file (numéro de contribuable) for IRC, ICC and IF purposes; (iv) the AEDT registers the company for VAT and issues the Luxembourg VAT identification number (n° d'identification TVA, prefixed LU) on submission of Form 5150 (demande d'immatriculation à la TVA) together with certified articles, RCS extract, manager identity documents and a description of the defense-tactical-vehicle manufacturing activity; registration is mandatory before any taxable supply is made or whenever annual taxable turnover reaches the EUR 35,000 threshold. For a non-resident entity with no Luxembourg seat or permanent establishment, separate procedures apply: OSS (One-Stop-Shop) registration for intra-EU distance sales/remote services, or direct AEDT registration via Form 5152 with a Luxembourg VAT fiscal representative (représentant fiscal responsable) where the non-resident carries out taxable supplies in Luxembourg and is established outside the EU; EU VAT-refund claims are filed electronically under Directive 2008/9/EC through the Member State's portal, while third-country refund claims follow the 13th Directive procedure before the AEDT.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation. The SARL is a Luxembourg-resident capital company (société de capitaux) with legal personality, limited liability and fully paid minimum capital of EUR 12,000; it is a taxable person in its own right and is not eligible for pass-through treatment under Luxembourg domestic law. The SARL is subject to entity-level corporate income tax (impôt sur le revenu des collectivités, IRC) at a 17% national headline rate, the municipal business tax (impôt commercial communal, ICC) at rates of 3.5%-6.75% (Luxembourg City: 6.75%), the 7% solidarity surcharge on IRC, and the net wealth tax (impôt sur la fortune, IF) of 0.5% on qualifying net assets above the statutory EUR 2 million allowance (with a progressive IF schedule for large balance sheets and a minimum annual IF of EUR 536). The combined corporate income-plus-municipal headline rate approximates 24.94%. Income is taxed on a worldwide basis, with credit relief for foreign-source income and territorial sourcing only for permanent establishments and treaty-protected situations. A domestic participation exemption (≥10% or ≥EUR 1.2 million acquisition cost, 12-month holding period) is available at the entity level, and the SARL may benefit from the toolbox of Luxembourg holding-company regimes only where the operational manufacturing profile permits.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Luxembourg does not provide a US-style check-the-box election; entity classification is fixed by statute and tax treaties. The relevant statutory election mechanisms include: (i) the integrated tax-group (consolidation) election under Article 164bis LIR for affiliates held directly or indirectly at ≥95%, producing a single tax base for Luxembourg-resident group members, with an irrevocable 5-year commitment; (ii) the participation-exemption application, together with the anti-hybrid alignment option introduced by the ATAD-transposing Law of 25 March 2020, under which a Luxembourg entity caught by hybrid or reverse-hybrid mismatch outcomes (e.g., where the foreign ultimate parent treats the SARL as transparent) may elect to align its Luxembourg characterization so as to prevent double deduction or deduction-without-inclusion mismatches; (iii) the VAT option to tax real-estate lettings (Article 48 of the VAT Law) for the industrial facility; (iv) the OSS Union/Non-Union scheme elections for intra-EU distance sales and remote services; (v) the customs Registered Exporter (REX) self-certification election for preferential-origin declarations on third-country export; and (vi) the Peppol/Factur-X access-point registration election for mandatory B2G e-invoicing. Each election requires a written application to the competent authority (ACD, AEDT or Customs) and, where applicable, a shareholder agreement or statutory board resolution.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque centrale du Luxembourg (BCL), the national central bank of the Eurosystem operating under the monetary policy framework of the European Central Bank (ECB); prudential and AML supervision of credit institutions in Luxembourg is exercised by the Commission de Surveillance du Secteur Financier (CSSF).
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: The euro is fully convertible on both current and capital account. Capital movements, payments, and profit remittances are unrestricted under Article 63 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union (TFEU) and Directive 88/361/EEC; no Luxembourg foreign-exchange authorisation or capital-transfer licence is required for equity injections, trade settlements, or dividend distributions. The practical hurdles are non-FX frictions: (i) dividend distributions to non-resident shareholders trigger Luxembourg dividend withholding tax (15% statutory domestic rate, reduced to 0% for qualifying EU parent companies under the Parent-Subsidiary Directive, or reduced under tax treaties); (ii) all cross-border flows must be declared to the BCL by the resident bank via the monthly Balance of Payments return, which creates an administrative checkpoint; (iii) military-hardware payments are subject to CSSF enhanced due diligence and EU/UN/OFAC sanctions screening, and flows from state procurement entities in embargoed countries can be frozen even though the euro itself is fully convertible.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Luxembourg imposes no statutory surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export proceeds; exporters may freely retain EUR, USD, or third-currency receivables on their accounts and convert at market rates. The only regulatory obligations are: (i) the bank's monthly BCL Balance of Payments filing of the proceeds under the correct purpose code; and (ii) for ISIC 3040 military-vehicle exports, a valid export authorisation from the Luxembourg Ministry of Economy under the EU Common Military List, Directive 2009/43/EC for intra-EU transfers, and the Luxembourg export-control law for dual-use items on Regulation (EU) 2021/821; expiry or revocation of the authorisation operates as a de facto blockage of liquidation of export receivables.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational multi-currency account / Capital Escrow (compte bloqué) account
Operational multi-currency account / Capital Escrow (compte bloqué) account
Operational EUR/USD current account and secondary clearing account

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BANQUE ET CAISSE D'ÉPARGNE DE L'ÉTAT (BCEE)

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.account_class: Operational current account; no defence-sector LC or credit facility

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Low-Medium viability. Luxembourg law authorises CSSF-licensed payment institutions and e-money institutions (EMIs) under PSD2 and permits fully digital remote onboarding; however, global EMIs (Wise, Revolut, Payoneer and similar) commonly decline ISIC 3040 military-tactical hardware accounts, cannot issue or advise UCP600 documentary credits, cannot process diplomatic-government instructs, and lack correspondent depth for defence-sector sanctions risk. Under the Luxembourg EMI regime, client funds are subject to safeguarding and segregation only and EMIs may not grant commercial credit. Recommended role: a secondary, non-critical disbursement rail for minor operational supplier payments after receipt of the statutory special export licence and acceptance by a tier-1 commercial bank.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote digital onboarding is legally permissible under CSSF electronic-identification guidelines, but for a High_Risk_Special_License defence-hardware manufacturer, the effective bank mandate is physical presence: the statutory gérant(s)/managers, all directors, and natural-person beneficial owners (or one resident holder of a fully notarised power of attorney) must attend an in-person KYC interview at the bank's Luxembourg premises, present original identification and the notarised constitutive deed, and sign the account mandate. The interview will include an end-use narrative, verification of the military export licence, and a review of government counterparties, freight forwarders, and brokers. Failure or refusal of physical attendance by the controlling persons is an automatic declinature trigger under the bank's internal defence-sector policy.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Registration of a high-risk Annex II activity (NACE 30.40 / ISIC 3040 — manufacture of military armoured vehicles) on the Luxembourg Trade and Companies Register (RCS), automatically categorising the client as high-risk under the Luxembourg AML Law of 28 July 2020 and invoking mandatory enhanced due diligence.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: (i) certified copy of the statutory export authorisation issued by the Luxembourg Ministry of Economy for the specific armoured-vehicle model; (ii) an active government procurement contract or diplomatic purchase order; (iii) signed End-User Certificate (EUC) and Import Certificate/Delivery Verification Certificate from the destination state; (iv) ISIC/NACE registration excerpt from the RCS acknowledging the defence scope; (v) an internal AML compliance programme with named AML/CFT officer.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident UBO chain and opaque source-of-funds for the €12,000 minimum SARL capital escrow deposit; bank internal policy requires proof of economic substance and legitimacy of every contributory euro before opening a blocked capital account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: (i) notarised share-subscription deed; (ii) blocked-funds certificate issued by the receiving Luxembourg credit institution; (iii) six months of bank statements of the contributing shareholder and, where available, three years of audited financial statements; (iv) LEI certificate (549300LUX) and RCS extract; (v) beneficial-ownership extract from the Luxembourg Register of Beneficial Owners (RBE); (vi) source-of-wealth letters for every UBO.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions and watchlist hits on counterparties, freight forwarders, brokers, or jurisdiction of the ultimate government buyer; the defence sector triggers mandatory screening against the EU Consolidated List, UN sanctions, and OFAC SDN list in respect of any USD clearing leg.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: (i) final false-positive disposition reports from compliant World-Check or similar screening; (ii) legal memorandum from a Luxembourg or international counsel confirming the counterparty is not a designated person; (iii) official end-user letter on state letterhead; (iv) confirmation that the goods are not on the EU/UN embargo lists and that the export licence covers the specific model; (v) a signed non-diversion clause and delivery-verification undertaking from the end-user.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: SWIFT purpose-code mismatch or BCL BOP misdeclaration — e.g., a payment involving a foreign ministry or defence procurement agency coded inconsistently with the BCL balance-of-payments matrix, triggering a freeze, a suspicious-transaction report, and de-risking withdrawal of the account.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Dossier bundle: (i) compliance-approved SWIFT/ISO 20022 purpose code (e.g., 'EQUI' for equity injection or the appropriate goods-trade code for export proceeds) matched to the underlying contract; (ii) the underlying signed contract and commercial invoice; (iii) the bank's Defence-Desk pre-approval memo; (iv) UCP600-compliant documentary credit terms proving a lawful trade in military equipment; (v) a BCL BOP submission template completed by the client under the bank's guidance to eliminate coding mismatches.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: Inbound EUR injection is executed by SWIFT/gpi wire from each subscribing shareholder to the SARL's notarial blocked-funds account (compte bloqué) or a dedicated Capital Escrow Account at the Luxembourg credit institution, using ISO 20022 purpose code 'EQUI' (equity capital) in the structured remittance; the aggregate must cover the statutory minimum share capital of €12,000 fully paid. The receiving bank completes the BCL Balance of Payments declaration under category A (direct investment — equity), and the blocked funds are released only upon production of the notarial deed and the RCS registration excerpt. USD injections are converted on a spot basis via the correspondent bank, with the same purpose code, and the U.S. clearing leg is screened against OFAC SDN. For verification, the bank requires the LEI (549300LUX), shareholder corporate extracts, passport copies, and source-of-funds evidence for every contributor.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: EUR disbursements below €100,000 settle through SEPA Credit Transfer or SEPA Instant; high-value EUR payments are cleared in real time through T2 (successor to TARGET2); USD trade settlements use CHIPS/Fedwire via the bank's New York correspondent with SWIFT.gpi MT103 / ISO 20022 pacs.008 messages. For defence procurements, the primary rails are irrevocable documentary Letter of Credit (LC) transactions under UCP600, typically issued by the buyer's bank and confirmed by the Luxembourg confirming bank only against 100% cash cover; Diplomatic LC instructions from foreign ministries are advised via the BNP Paribas or Société Générale government-correspondent network and paid only upon presentation of the export licence, End-User Certificate, transport documents, and a clean inspection certificate. Each outflow is declared to the BCL under balance-of-payments category B (goods), and every USD or euro leg is screened against EU/UN/OFAC consolidated lists before release.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Vanilla deliverable OTC FX forwards (EUR/USD, EUR/GBP) under an ISDA/CSA master agreement, restricted to hedging committed USD/GBP receivables with no speculative positions
OTC FX swaps (EUR/USD) for working-capital conversion, sequencing of payables and receivables, and balance-sheet liquidity management
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) in limited-access currencies (CNY, INR, KRW) where physical delivery is legally or administratively restricted, with underlying trade-contract documentation required
Cross-currency interest rate swaps (EUR/USD CCIRS) for long-term financing hedges linked to multi-year government procurement and export-credit arrangements

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 24.94% (Luxembourg City aggregate: 17% corporate income tax + 1.19% solidarity surcharge + 6.75% municipal business tax)
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: The Luxembourg IP box regime provides an 80% exemption on qualifying patent and software-derived gross income, reducing the effective rate to approximately 4.99%; a participation exemption on qualifying dividends and capital gains applies to shareholdings of at least 10% or EUR 1.2 million acquisition value held for 12 months; government-approved investment tax credits (8-12% of qualifying investment cost) and an innovation tax credit may apply to an armored tactical vehicle production line.
corporate_income_tax_regime.tax_loss_carryforward_limit_years: Unlimited (annual carryforward set-off is limited to 70% of positive taxable income, with the first EUR 100,000 of taxable profit excluded from the cap for small taxpayers)

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Form 720 (corporate income tax, IRC) and Form 730 (municipal business tax, ICC) submitted via MyGuichet.lu electronic portal or through the Luxembourg direct tax administration's secure ESDI platform by a registered tax advisor.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Annual returns must be filed no later than 31 December of the calendar year following the close of the tax year (e.g., FYE 31 December 2024 due by 31 December 2025); extensions are technically available only on a reasoned written request prior to the deadline, but in practice late-filing interest runs from 1 January of the second year following the accounting year.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Luxembourg TIN, legal name, registered office, ISIC/NACE code (3040 for armored vehicle manufacture), fiscal year start and end dates, incorporation date and number of days in the first tax accounting period.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: For a non-resident with a Luxembourg permanent establishment (PE), enter the local branch's separate TIN and the PE's address; resident SARL entities enter the central company data and indicate the local defense-regulatory licence number.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 2 – Reconciliation of book income to taxable income
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Reconciliation from statutory profit per the approved annual accounts to the taxable base; add-back of non-deductible expenses (e.g., 50% of motor-vehicle, entertainment, and certain royalty charges if related to extraterritorial use), and deduction of exempt participation dividends and IP-box-eligible net revenues.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: The PE must present a Luxembourg-prepared standalone balance sheet and profit-and-loss statement; reconciliation is restricted to assets and transactions booked to the PE, not the foreign head office.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 3 – Participation exemption and dividend deduction
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Claim for excluded income from dividends and capital gains on qualifying shareholding; must satisfy the 12-month holding period and 10% or EUR 1.2 million cost threshold, evidenced by a share register certificate and securities account statement.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PE owners claiming the exemption on investment income must demonstrate that the paid-in capital and holding entity books reside in the Luxembourg PE balance sheet.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Computation of the 80% exemption for qualifying IP revenues that directly arise from patents, copyrighted design software and qualifying licensed royalty income, after deducting directly allocatable costs and depreciation of R&D assets; the net IP income must be supported by election schedules using the specific commercial methodology.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-residents seeking treaty relief must show that the legal title and day-to-day administration of the tactical-vehicle CAD software are held and managed by the Luxembourg PE.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Offset of recognized loss years brought forward under the 70% annual cap; amounts are automatically calculated by the tax software once prior assessments are entered.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: A PE may use only historical losses that were taxed in Luxembourg and that arose from the same PE commercial activity, subject to the 70% statutory ceiling.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 6 – Tax calculated and municipal business tax coefficient
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Application of the 17% statutory CIT rate and 7% solidarity surcharge to the taxable base, then allocation of the municipal business tax at the municipality-appropriate coefficient (6.75% for Luxembourg City); the final amount due is net of prepayments made in the four quarterly instalments.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident PEs are assessed on the PE's taxable earning power under the same rates and coefficient; only Luxembourg source profits are included.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing triggers an automatic 10% tax increase on the assessed amount after the statutory deadline; a further 20% increase can be applied after a formal reminder. Late-payment interest accrues at 0.6% per month (7.2% annual). Failure to file by the maximum 31 December deadline can lead to ex officio assessment, administrative penalties up to EUR 5,000, and where intent is proven, criminal fines up to EUR 100,000 and up to 5 years' imprisonment.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To obtain a reduced dividend withholding tax rate or an exemption, the non-resident shareholder must submit an application to the Luxembourg direct tax administration using Form Rozar/CTA (or the CF4C equivalent), accompanied by an original tax residency certificate (TRC) issued by the shareholder's domestic revenue authority within the same calendar year, together with proof of beneficial ownership and the shareholding tenancy records. The application must be filed no later than three years after the end of the calendar year in which the dividend became payable. For the full participation exemption under the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive, the shareholder must annex a statement showing it is subject to corporate income tax and is resident in the EU, in addition to the standard TRC.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: statutory 0% withholding tax under Luxembourg domestic law; DTA reduction is generally 0% for beneficial owners resident in treaty states, irrespective of the participation threshold. Interest: statutory 0% withholding tax on ordinary cross-border arm's-length interest; there is no Luxembourg withholding tax on debenture or note interest. Payments to connected lenders under a profit-participating feature may be re-characterized as dividends and subject to 15% withholding.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: Mandatory Master File is required where the consolidated group global revenue reaches EUR 50,000,000. A Local File is additionally required when the Luxembourg entity's aggregate related-party transactions for the fiscal year exceed EUR 100,000, or where the entity is engaged in intra-group procurement of vehicle hulls, software licenses, royalty payments or service fees under the LU-LU SARL. Regardless of thresholds, the Luxembourg tax administration may demand contemporaneous transfer pricing documentation on any cross-border transaction.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: Luxembourg applies the economic substance doctrine through the general anti-abuse provisions derived from the EU ATAD and OECD BEPS Action 5, together with the Luxembourg administrative commentary on Abusive Transactions (Circular LIR n° 46 of 2017). Although a defense-hardware manufacturer is not a geographically mobile ring-fenced entity, a resident SARL must demonstrate physical premises with actual armored-vehicle assembly operations, qualified defense-engineering staff in Luxembourg, locally exercised board and executive management decisions, procurement and treasury functions, and active operational bank accounts. Without such substance, the tax authority can deny corporate residence, disregard the SARL as a letterbox entity, re-attribute its defense contracts and resulting income to the controlling non-resident parent, and disallow treaty benefits, the participation exemption and the IP regime. Defense export licensing records under the 2016 Luxembourg law on military equipment and dual-use items are part of the commercial substance dossier.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberately understating annual production revenues from all-terrain military tactical vehicles, recording false export invoices, misclassifying intangible asset sales to a related company as royalty relief, or pre-paying inflated freight charges to a foreign shell entity to create non-deductible expenses.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Criminal tax fraud under the Luxembourg Income Tax Law and the General Tax Act: fine of up to EUR 100,000 and imprisonment of up to 5 years; civil reassessment with a 20% tax increase and monthly default interest at 0.6%; confiscation of evaded profit attributable to the fraudulent invoices.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors of the SARL are jointly and severally liable for the unpaid corporate tax and interest if the misstatement leads to insolvency or liquidation; the Public Prosecutor's Office can issue an international arrest warrant and prohibit travel from Luxembourg pending the investigation.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell company / lack of economic substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a Luxembourg SARL as a pure invoicing shell with no physical manufacturing or engineering activity; all marketing, procurement and negotiation decisions are made by the American or German parent; the registered office is merely the address of a fiduciary provider.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: The Luxembourg tax authorities may deny the claimed residence and treaty benefits, reclassify the profits of the SARL as an unlicensed permanent establishment of the shareholder, and impose a 5% administrative surcharge on the full amount of income deemed misattributed; the participation exemption may be retroactively reversed if the letters of intent for the 12-month holding period are absent.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The corporate veil is pierced and the directors become personally taxable on the earnings of the SARL; they can be ordered to reinstate a physical industrial presence within 90 days; failure results in deregistration from the Luxembourg Register of Commerce and a court order prohibiting the director from serving on any other board within the EEA.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: AML / defense and dual-use sanctions breach
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Processing government direct wires and diplomatic letters of credit for armored tactical vehicles without the LCL-approved defense export license, exceeding the offensive-use limits of the arms embargo, or making payments to a sanctioned defense ministry or to entities on the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions List.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Administrative fine up to EUR 250,000 per prohibited transaction and confiscation of the full payment proceeds under Luxembourg Anti-Money Laundering Law; the SARL is additionally blacklisted on the CSSF/WMD list, which prohibits any EU counterpart from transacting with it.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors have direct criminal liability under Article 506-1 of the Luxembourg Criminal Code, punishable by 5 to 10 years' imprisonment and a fine of EUR 100,000 to EUR 1 million; an automatic director disqualification for 10 years arises; the court may freeze all bank accounts of the director and the SARL and appoint a receiver without prior notice.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Transfer pricing documentation and adjustment failure
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Selling armored tactical vehicles to a UAE trading affiliate at 35% below market price and purchasing Slovak-combat hull modules from an affiliated supplier at 40% above the TP benchmark, without preparing a local file or comparable search; the company engages in an undocumented inflated service fee payment to the parent company.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment on an arm's length basis with a 50% penalty on the additional corporate tax assessed; if the TP documentation is not produced, a fixed penalty of 10% of the total intercompany transaction value is levied; interest runs at 0.6% per month.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: The directors who requested or approved the pricing distortion are personally liable for the tax deficiency; in an aggravated case, the court can order the production of all internal e-mails through a third-party discovery order and impose a travel ban on the Luxembourg-based director during the administrative examination.
